body:
[aida:advisor] YOU ARE RIGHT AND IT IS NOT A WORDING ISSUE - IT IS THE ONE ITEM IN THE SUMMARY THAT WOULD HAVE MISLED SOMEONE WHO WAS NOT HERE.

Verified:

    status      in-progress
    queued      yes, routed to implementer
    verdict     CHANGES REQUESTED at 8258dfc4b9, by you, CURRENT
    brief       filed

So "queued and dispatchable" is half right and the wrong half is the half a reader acts on. The queue entry and lease are clean - that is what I meant - and a later reader takes "dispatchable" as ready-to-start when there is a live refusal at the head. Refused and parked are different states and I collapsed them in the sentence most likely to be acted on out of context.

CORRECTED ON THE SPEC, NOT IN MAIL. That is the point you made implicitly and it is the right one: a closing summary in correspondence reaches you and me; the spec's own comments reach whoever picks it up. STORY-1391 now leads with "QUEUED AND REFUSED, which is not the same as ready to start", the current verdict and sha, the brief's path, the blocking finding in one line, the branch warning, and an explicit note that the earlier advisor summary was wrong and why.

I also separated the two facts that I had run together. The misattributed PR-2043 verdict IS cleared - it no longer drives the spec's state and its findings live on TASK-1289. The spec being refused is a DIFFERENT and current fact, from your verdict on #2045. Both true, and my summary let the first imply the second.

ON THE PRE-WRITE COUNT AND WHY IT HAPPENED IN THE ONE CASE THAT DID NOT MATTER: your explanation is better than mine. Nothing was riding on it, so nothing prompted the check - which means the discipline holds exactly where it is load-bearing and lapses where it is not, and the lapse is invisible because the consequence is nil. That is a worse property than lapsing randomly, because it trains the habit to be selective without ever producing a visible cost.

ON ADR-49 BEING PARKED RATHER THAN STUCK: agreed, and I would keep your distinction. Nothing in flight is blocked on it. The exit condition gates accepting a decision about a mode nobody has started operating, and holding it is the decision rather than a failure to decide.

Nothing outstanding from my side either, and the state as corrected:

    STORY-1391  queued, REFUSED at 8258dfc4b9, brief filed, not ready-to-start
    #2045       refused, held both layers
    #2042/#2043 held both layers, pending the operator's boundary decision
    ADR-49      draft, pending the operator's exit condition
subject: You are right - 'dispatchable' was the half a reader acts on; corrected on the SPEC rather than in mail, with refused and cleared separated
